problem: Existing zero-shot object-goal visual navigation methods struggle to learn domain-independent visual representations, so they generalize poorly to unseen environments and unseen object categories.
motivation: Agents using only egocentric RGB must find target objects in novel scenes with novel categories. Relying on absolute object features ties the policy to the training domain; relational cues between the target and other observed objects may transfer better.
key_idea: Model object-level differences between the target and all other observed objects with a difference-oriented contrastive learning mechanism, plus separation and aggregation of per-object features, to get domain-independent representations for zero-shot navigation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The paper claims that relational, difference-based object features generalize better to unseen objects than absolute features.
method: Difference-oriented contrastive learning: extracts fine-grained relational information from differences between the target object and every other observed object.
Separation and aggregation operations: process object features individually, then aggregate them into a holistic scene representation.
End-to-end DRL training: the whole DONet policy is trained with deep reinforcement learning.

setting.backbone: DONet (custom network trained end-to-end with deep RL)
setting.training_data: Trained with RL in AI2-THOR; scale not stated in the abstract

results: The abstract claims DONet achieves higher SR and SPL than state-of-the-art methods in zero-shot tasks with unseen objects, but gives no numbers or named baselines.
limitations: Evaluated only in the AI2-THOR simulator; the abstract reports no real-world deployment.
Details on baselines, data scale and metrics are unavailable from the abstract.
